© SpaceX — Long-term crewed Mars architecture per Elon Musk's IAC presentations (2016 / 2017 / 2024) and SpaceX Mars program statements. Round-trip enabled by ISRU propellant production on the Mars surface (CH₄ + LOX from CO₂ + H₂O). Date is illustrative — the 2031 Mars launch window is one of several long-term targets discussed by SpaceX; actual schedule depends on Starship maturation, prior cargo missions, and ISRU validation. Round-trip arc is the conceptual architecture, not a flight plan. On 2026-02-08 Musk said work on Mars would start in about five to seven years (CNN); the 2031 date predates that and no new date has been set.
Musk clips his Mars settlement ambition, aims for the moon instead — CNN (2026-02-09)
SpaceX's proposed crewed round trip to Mars

SpaceX's long-term crewed Mars architecture as outlined in Elon Musk's 2016, 2017, and 2024 IAC presentations. A Starship lifts off from Earth fully fuelled in low-Earth orbit via a fleet of refilling tanker flights, performs trans-Mars injection, and lands a crew of roughly 10 with cargo and ISRU equipment on the Martian surface. Return-leg propellant (methane + liquid oxygen) is manufactured on Mars from atmospheric CO₂ and subsurface water ice via the Sabatier process, enabling the same Starship to lift off again, perform trans-Earth injection, and return the crew. Round-trip duration depends on the launch window and surface stay; the illustrative timeline shown here is ~2.5 years door-to-door (213 days outbound, ~500-day surface stay, return on the next favourable window). The architecture is conceptual — date and parameters subject to substantial revision pending Starship maturation and ISRU validation. In February 2026 Musk said work on Mars would start in about five to seven years; the 2031 date shown here predates that, and no new date has been set.
